issues.description: The problem statement requires Bookstore to hold an array of Book and to provide an initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]) (problem statement lines 8–12). The solution instead declares Bookstore.books as Set<Book> and implements init(books: Set<Book>) (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 9–16). This is a cross-artifact type mismatch: students implementing the constructor as specified by the problem (taking [Book]) will not match the solution's constructor, and automated tests or graders that expect the array-based signature will fail or be confused.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution match the problem statement: change Bookstore.books to be an Array ([Book]) and change the initializer to init(books: [Book]). Alternatively, if Set is desired, update the problem statement to require Set<Book> (and document the reason), but prefer using [Book] to match the exercise text.

issues.description: The solution's Client.assembleBookstore builds a local variable books as [Book] and then returns Bookstore(books: books) (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift lines 31–57). That call is inconsistent with the solution's Bookstore initializer which expects a Set<Book> (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 14–16). Passing an Array where a Set is expected is a type mismatch and will not compile. This is a constructor-parameter incompatibility between how the caller constructs the Bookstore and the Bookstore initializer signature in the solution.
issues.suggested_fix: If Bookstore should accept an Array (as the problem specifies), change the Bookstore initializer to init(books: [Book]) so Client.assembleBookstore can pass the array directly. If Set is intended, change the call site to convert the array into a set when returning (e.g. return Bookstore(books: Set(books))). Prefer aligning solution to the problem statement (use [Book]).

issues.description: Within the solution, Bookstore stores a Set<Book> (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 9–12), but the Book struct in the same solution does not conform to Hashable (solution_repository/Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 24–33). Using a Set requires its element type to conform to Hashable; as written this is an internal inconsistency in the solution that will prevent compilation.
issues.suggested_fix: Either change Bookstore.books to an Array ([Book]) (preferred to match the problem statement), or make Book conform to Hashable (e.g. declare `struct Book: Hashable { ... }` and ensure equality/hash semantics are appropriate) if Set<Book> is required. Ensure all usages and the initializer are updated consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement requires Bookstore to hold an array of Books and specifies the initializer signature init(books: [Book]). In the solution repository the Bookstore stores its collection as a Set<Book> and the initializer is init(books: Set<Book>). Although the identifier name 'books' is the same, the collection type and initializer parameter type differ between problem and solution. This mismatch can confuse students (they are told to use an array), may change expected semantics (ordering, duplicates), and will make direct mapping from the problem’s API to the provided solution unclear.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the collection type consistent. Either: (A) Update the solution to match the problem statement by using an Array: change the property to `let books: [Book]` and the initializer to `init(books: [Book])`; or (B) if a Set is intentional, update the problem statement (and any tests/documentation) to require a Set<Book> so students are given a consistent API to implement.
